articles.title: Monchi aprieta el botón del pánico
articles.standfirst: El Espanyol prescindió de los servicios de Manolo González tras la eliminación en Copa del Rey contra el Sestao
articles.summary: El Espanyol prescindió de los servicios de Manolo González tras la eliminación en Copa del Rey contra el Sestao
articles.body: La situación del Espanyol lleva meses siendo preocupante. La pasada temporada, el conjunto perico pasó de soñar con meterse en Europa a pelear hasta el final por evitar el descenso. Pese a ello, la directiva decidió mantener su confianza en Manolo González, el técnico que había devuelto al equipo a Primera en 2024. Sin embargo, los resultados no han acompañado y la situación parece haberse enquistado hasta el punto de que Monchi ha decidido apretar el botón del pánico para tratar de enderezar el rumbo de una temporada que empieza a complicarse demasiado pronto. La decisión de prescindir del entrenador llegó después de la eliminación en la Copa del Rey frente al Sestao, conjunto de Segunda Federación. Un golpe difícil de digerir para una afición que esperaba que el torneo copero sirviera para recuperar sensaciones y cambiar la dinámica. La derrota terminó por precipitar una decisión que llevaba tiempo barruntándose en los despachos, con un equipo que no encontraba la manera de levantar el vuelo. Los números en Liga explican buena parte de la decisión. El Espanyol acumula cinco jornadas consecutivas sin ganar y apenas ha sumado un punto de los últimos 15 posibles. Una racha que le ha llevado a cerrar la jornada 10 en puestos de descenso y que ha terminado por agotar el crédito de Manolo González. El margen de reacción empieza a reducirse y el club necesita encontrar cuanto antes una solución que permita recuperar la confianza y alejarse de una zona baja que vuelve a amenazar con convertirse en una pesadilla. Pese a este escenario, 777 todavía no sitúa al Espanyol entre los tres principales candidatos a perder la categoría. Su descenso cotiza a 4.50, por encima de equipos como el Málaga, con una cuota de 1.50; el Racing, a 2.38; el Getafe, a 3.50; y el Valencia y el Levante, ambos a 4.0. No obstante, hay un precedente que invita a la cautela: el Espanyol ha firmado su peor arranque liguero desde la temporada 2019-20, cuando también acumulaba ocho puntos después de 10 jornadas y acabó perdiendo la categoría. Las apuestas deportivas reflejan que todavía hay margen para reaccionar, pero el equipo necesita transformar esa posibilidad en resultados. A la espera de que Monchi anuncie quién será el sustituto de Manolo González, el objetivo pasa por cortar la mala dinámica cuanto antes. No será una tarea sencilla, ya que el próximo compromiso llevará al Espanyol hasta La Cerámica para medirse al Villarreal. Los pericos necesitarán dar un paso al frente ante un rival exigente si quieren empezar a salir del pozo. 777 paga a 6.40 la victoria blanquiazul. Una cuota que refleja la dificultad del desafío. Las mejores casas de apuestas seguirán pendientes de la reacción del equipo, que necesita un cambio de rumbo urgente para evitar que la temporada vuelva a convertirse en una lucha agónica por la permanencia.

articles.title: Alcaraz busca un nuevo logro
articles.standfirst: Para Tonybet es el favorito a alzarse con el título en Viena, por primera vez
articles.summary: Para Tonybet es el favorito a alzarse con el título en Viena, por primera vez
articles.body: El Erste Bank Open, ATP 500 que se disputa en pista dura cubierta del Wiener Stadthalle entre el 26 de octubre y el 1 de noviembre, reúne esta semana a seis jugadores del top 10. Es un torneo que sirve de ensayo para el tramo final de la temporada, con el Masters 1000 de París y las ATP Finals en el horizonte, y varios tenistas se juegan algo más que el trofeo. Un cambio de última hora en el calendario, provocado por el aplazamiento del Six Kings Slam, ha traído a la capital austriaca a uno de los grandes nombres del circuito. Las casas de apuestas ya tienen claro quién manda en el mercado. Para Tonybet, Carlos Alcaraz es el favorito, con una cuota de 1.95 que lo sitúa casi como un candidato a ganar de cada dos opciones. Llega a Viena por primera vez desde 2021, cuando cayó ante Zverev, y nunca ha levantado este título. Con un balance de 33 victorias y cinco derrotas en la temporada, busca su cuarto título del año y el número 28 de su carrera. La cuota refleja su jerarquía, aunque también algo de confianza ajena. El murciano aún busca su mejor versión en pista cubierta y tiene un cuadro nada sencillo. Debutó ante Karen Khachanov y su camino pasa por posibles duelos con Tommy Paul en cuartos y con Medvedev o Mensik en semifinales. A no mucha distancia en las apuestas deportivas, aparece Alexander Zverev, a cuota 3.99. El alemán es cabeza de serie número uno, excampeón de Viena y llega con la opción de alcanzar por primera vez en su carrera el número uno del mundo si los resultados le acompañan. Conoce bien esta pista y, tras un debut duro ante Martín Landaluce, afronta un cuadro con Cobolli, De Miñaur y Tiafoe en su mitad. Al estar en el lado contrario, solo podría cruzarse con Alcaraz en la final, un enfrentamiento que el mercado da casi por hecho. Alex de Miñaur cotiza a 9.96. El australiano es quinto cabeza de serie y ocupa el puesto ocho del ranking, con un tenis sólido y muy regular, especialmente efectivo en pistas rápidas. Su camino pasa por la zona de Zverev, un obstáculo importante que el mercado ya tiene en cuenta. Es un jugador que rara vez da un mal partido, aunque le suele faltar el punto extra para ganar grandes finales ante los mejores. Daniil Medvedev comparte esa misma cuota, 9.96. El ruso es tercer cabeza de serie, ocupa el quinto puesto mundial y se encuentra en plena lucha por un billete a las ATP Finals, lo que le obliga a sumar puntos. Su juego plano y su fortaleza en pista dura cubierta le convierten en un rival incómodo para cualquiera, y su posible duelo con Alcaraz en semifinales sería uno de los grandes alicientes del torneo. A su favor juega el hecho de que su cuota recoge a un jugador con experiencia en las rondas finales, pero también la irregularidad que ha mostrado esta temporada. Cierra la lista de aspirantes Tommy Paul, a 14.9. El estadounidense, séptimo cabeza de serie, aparece en la misma zona del cuadro que Alcaraz, con quien podría verse las caras en cuartos de final. Es un jugador capaz de poner en apuros a cualquiera cuando su saque funciona, pero su cuota refleja que el mercado lo ve como un rival para frenar al favorito, más que como un candidato real al título. articles.title: Los Brewers se estrenan como campeones de las Series Mundiales
articles.standfirst: Milwaukee gana por primera vez la MLB después de vencer en el quinto encuentro a los Rays 1-4 y firmar un curso histórico: mejor equipo en la temporada regular y 11-2 en los playoffs
articles.summary: Milwaukee gana por primera vez la MLB después de vencer en el quinto encuentro a los Rays 1-4 y firmar un curso histórico: mejor equipo en la temporada regular y 11-2 en los playoffs
articles.body: Milwaukee Bravos ganó las Series Mundiales en 1957 de la mano de Hank Aaron, leyenda del béisbol. Pero aquel campeonato no sirvió de mucho en la ciudad de Wisconsin. Los Bravos finalmente se mudaron a Atlanta, donde siguen. Desde entonces, 58 años, Milwaukee no había tenido un campeón en el deporte más americano para los estadounidenses. Hasta hace unas horas, culminando una temporada histórica, los Brewers, fundados en 1969, consiguieron el triunfo en el Tropicana Field de St. Petersburg (Florida) tras vencer 1-4 a los Rays para alcanzar el primer título de su historia en la edición 123ª de las Series Mundiales. El venezolano William Contreras, campeón del Clásico Mundial con su país, fue elegido MVP. "Es el mejor equipo de la MLB contra el que he jugado y llevo siete temporadas en la Liga", dijo Drew Rasmussen, abridor de los Rays. La impresión no es exagerada, incluso pensando en el dominio de los Dodgers en 2024 y 2025. Los Brewers fueron el mejor equipo en temporada regular con 103 y cuando el mundo del béisbol profesional pensaba que no podían mejorar, Milwaukee ha firmado unos playoffs aplastantes con un balance de 11-2. Desde septiembre, cuando la temporada se pone 'seria', el equipo dirigido por Pat Murphy ha ganado 26 de 31 partidos. “Pienso en la ciudad de Milwaukee, en el estado de Wisconsin. Sin duda, nos impulsaron a seguir adelante, y este grupo de muchachos, este equipo de 2026, será recordado para siempre. Se lo merecen, porque eran un verdadero equipo, y no podría estar más agradecido ni más orgulloso de ser parte de esto”, dijo el entrenador de 67 años (el más mayor del campeonato), que ha construido una máquina perfecta: los Brewers fueron el segundo en la temporada en número de carreras, quintos en bases robadas y primero en porcentaje de bases por bolas. Lideraron en promedio de bateo. En defensa, fueron segundos en efectividad colectiva. Los Brewers ganaron un título muy merecido después de fracasar hace 44 años en su primer y único intento en las Series Mundiales (cayeron 4-0 ante los Cardinals). Y dejaron de pertenecer al club de las franquicias que nunca han sido campeones. Allí siguen los Rays junto a Seattle Mariners, Colorado Rockies y San Diego Padres. Contreras fue elegido MVP. "No sé cómo lo hago, pero siempre estoy ahí", dijo el venezolano, que hace siete meses había ganado con su selección el Clásico Mundial tras derrotar a Estados Unidos. Los Brewers se ha convertido en el tercer equipo de la historia en conseguir el título y ganar 100 partidos y el primero en hacerlo desde los Mets en 1969. Wisconsin, frío y olvidado, es el tercer estado del país desde 2010 en ser campeón de la NBA (Bucks), NFL (Packers) y MLB (Brewers). Los otros dos son Massachusetts y California.

articles.title: Defending champ shoots 63 at Te Arai, leads Asia-Pacific Amateur by 3 in New Zealand
articles.summary: Defending champion Fifa Laopakdee fired an 8-under 63 to take a three-shot lead at the Asia-Pacific Amateur.
articles.body:
Fifa Laopakdee made history last fall becoming the first player from Thailand to win the Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship in Dubai. Now he's trying to become the second player to win consecutive AAC titles, and he's off to a thrilling start.

Laopakdee, a senior at Arizona State, fired a stellar 8-under 63 on Thursday at Te Arai Links in New Zealand to take a three-shot lead after the opening round. He carded seven birdies and an eagle, a hole out from 83 yards on the par-4 ninth hole.

"Couldn't ask for a better way to start the round," Laopakdee said. "8 under wasn't on my bingo card today but able to pull it off. It feels pretty amazing."

Laopakdee leads New Zealand native Joshua Bai, whose 66 featured six birdies and only one blemish on the scorecard. Kiwis Cooper Moore and Ryan Xie are tied for third at 4 under.

Laopakdee's round was one stroke shy of the championship scoring record (62). Last year, he won on the third playoff hole to lock up spots in the Masters and Open Championship.

This year, he's trying to join Hideki Matsuyama as the only players to win consecutive Asia-Pacific Amateur titles and the third golfer to win the championship twice.

"Definitely one of the best rounds I've played this year by far," Laopakdee said. "As I said in the press conference, I didn't have my best golf this year, and it's nice to see that I'm still capable of playing how I played today in this kind of condition."

Laopakdee's round was stellar, coming in the afternoon in windy conditions. At Te Arai, where a majority of holes have views of the Pacific Ocean, the wind is often a factor, but Laopakdee was able to fight through the wind and dominate the opening day.

Heading into the second round, the projected cut is 5 over. The top-60 players and ties will advance to the weekend.

The winner earns exemptions into the 2027 Masters and Open Championship at St Andrews.

Cameron Jourdan is an assistant editor of Golfweek, covering college and amateur golf, the PGA Tour and plenty more. Follow Cameron on X/Twitter (@Cam_Jourdan) or Instagram (@GolfweekJourdan).

articles.title: In Photos: Rodtang Shows Off His Firepower Ahead Of World Grand Prix Showdown With Nong-O
articles.summary: The former flyweight king puts his skills on display before the long-awaited clash of Thai icons.
articles.body:
Former ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Champion Rodtang "The Iron Man" Jitmuangnon gave the media a glimpse of his preparations during an open workout at Jitmuangnon Gym in Nonthaburi, Thailand, on Wednesday, October 28.

The 29-year-old Thai megastar displayed his trademark intensity as he sharpened his weapons ahead of his highly anticipated showdown with legendary former ONE Bantamweight Muay Thai World Champion Nong-O Hama .

The two icons will finally collide in the 2026-2027 ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Grand Prix quarterfinals at The Inner Circle 38 on Friday, November 13, live in Asia primetime from Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium, streaming exclusively for members at live.onefc.com .

Originally scheduled to meet at ONE 173 last November, Rodtang and Nong-O now have the opportunity to settle their unfinished business, with a place in the tournament semifinals and a step toward World Title glory at stake.

Rodtang: 'The Iron Man' Reloads For Another Shot At Gold

One of the most electrifying strikers in Muay Thai history, Rodtang has amassed 274 career victories and a 17-3 record in ONE Championship, captivating audiences with his relentless aggression, granite chin, and devastating punching combinations.

The #2-ranked flyweight Muay Thai contender previously ruled the division for five years, successfully defending his ONE World Title five times before being stripped of the crown in 2024.

Now, following his return to ONE Championship under a new contract earlier this year, the Jitmuangnon Gym representative is determined to reclaim his place at the summit.

His latest preparations have included intensive conditioning and training alongside fellow Thai standout Nuenglanlek Jitmuangnon , as he readies himself for a potentially career-defining battle with one of his childhood heroes.

Nong-O: A Childhood Idol Becomes A Formidable Rival

Standing in Rodtang's path is a man whose extraordinary career helped inspire an entire generation of Thai fighters.

At 39, Nong-O remains one of Muay Thai's most revered figures, with 268 professional victories and eight ONE Bantamweight Muay Thai World Title wins to his name.

The #3-ranked flyweight Muay Thai contender has since set his sights on becoming a two-division ONE World Champion, bringing his exceptional timing, technical mastery, and punishing right kicks into a new championship pursuit.

For Rodtang, the matchup carries special significance. He grew up admiring Nong-O's skills and considers the contest an opportunity to test himself against a master of the sport.

But once the opening bell rings, mutual respect will give way to fierce competition as two of Thailand's greatest modern strikers battle for a place in the Grand Prix semifinals.

Here are some photos of Rodtang from his October 28 open workout at Jitmuangnon Gym in Nonthaburi, Thailand.

articles.title: Maxx Crosby Has Strong Message Amid Raiders’ Four-Game Losing Streak
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are riding a four-game losing streak after starting the season 3-0. Moreover, it might be a now-or-never situation heading into Week 8...
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are riding a four-game losing streak after starting the season 3-0. Moreover, it might be a now-or-never situation heading into Week 8 against the New York Jets.

If the Silver and Black can get a win against New York, they get themselves back to .500. However, a loss against the Jets and the Raiders could see their losing streak go to six games, given that they'll face the San Francisco 49ers in their next contest.

Nonetheless, while there can be negativity around a losing streak, the Raiders' Maxx Crosby isn't allowing that to reach the team's dressing room, as he had a message for the doubters who don't believe Las Vegas can turn their situation around.

"You play to win," Crosby told reporters on Oct. 28. "We're playing to try to make the playoffs and win. That's what we do. I try not to pay attention to it. I feel like it's probably the least amount of attention I pay to all the outside noise. But negativity is just how our world operates these days, and that's what sells.

"If you want to be negative and not believe, then stay over there. Stay on that side because I know when things turn around or when you win, all those tough people just disappear, and then they come back when it's convenient. But that's just what life is like. That's how the world is, unfortunately."

Maxx Crosby: Team Is Using Doubters as Motivation

Moreover, Crosby relayed the message regarding the team being doubted that they can turn this situation around, which they are trying to use as fuel to motivate the team heading into Week 8.

"I know these guys in the locker room want to win so bad, but it doesn't mean you can't be optimistic," Crosby added. "You have to be optimistic [and] you have to love this game and put everything into it, even when everybody is against you and everyone thinks it's the same old story. You have to go win, and that's how you shut everybody up.

"So I love being doubted. I've been doubted my whole life, so keep it coming. I appreciate that. You just make it a bigger monster. I know this locker room is the same way. We're all extremely motivated, and I know guys are ready to go out there and shut everybody up."

Raiders, Cowboys Get Blockbuster Trade Idea

Meanwhile, the losing streak has allowed for the Crosby trade speculation to resurface. Recently, in an Oct. 27 video from 105.3 The FAN , former NFL offensive lineman Mark Schlereth was asked whether he would do a trade that involved Crosby and the Cowboys sending wideout George Pickens the other way, along with other parts, as part of a blockbuster trade.

"Oh yeah, would I do that? I'd do that in a heartbeat," Schlereth said. "I wouldn't even think twice about it. George Pickens will wow you with the spectacular. That dude will make some spectacular plays. He had the touchdown catch, which was phenomenal, right?

"He'll make those, but there'll be plenty of times during the course of the game when you'll put on the film and he's just standing around killing grass. So, yeah, would I do that? I would do that without even thinking twice about it."

articles.title: Why did the New Jersey Devils make a puzzling Connor Hellebuyck move just days after a blockbuster NHL trade
articles.summary: The New Jersey Devils made headlines by sidelining Connor Hellebuyck just days after acquiring him in a major trade, leaving fans wondering about the team's goaltending strategy and Hellebuyck's role moving forward.
articles.body: The New Jersey Devils raised questions about their goaltending plans after Connor Hellebuyck was left out of the lineup entirely for their game against the Colorado Avalanche. The decision came just one game after the star goalie made his first start for New Jersey following a major trade from Winnipeg.Jake Allen was named the starter, with Rémi Poirier serving as backup. The Devils did not publicly explain why Hellebuyck was given the night off, leaving his status a subject of speculation.Why New Jersey Devils rested Connor Hellebuyck after NHL debutThe New Jersey Devils gave Connor Hellebuyck a complete night off against the Colorado Avalanche, choosing Jake Allen to start and Rémi Poirier as the backup. The decision stood out because Hellebuyck had only just returned to game action in his first start for New Jersey.Devils reporter Amanda Stein reported before puck drop that Allen would start in goal, with Poirier backing him up. Hellebuyck was not listed as either the starter or backup, an unusual sight so soon after his arrival through a blockbuster trade.The decision prompted questions among fans, with some speculating about a possible injury. However, the available report did not confirm that Hellebuyck was hurt, and the Devils had not publicly offered a specific explanation for his absence. It would therefore be premature to describe the situation as an injury concern.Allen’s selection gave New Jersey an experienced option against Colorado. The veteran goaltender has a history of handling NHL starts, while Poirier provided the team’s backup option for the matchup.The decision also highlighted the importance of goaltending depth during a demanding regular-season schedule. Even after making a major move to acquire an established star, the Devils still need other goaltenders who can step in when required.What does the decision mean for Connor Hellebuyck’s future?Hellebuyck’s absence raises questions, but it does not establish that the Devils have concerns about his long-term role. A full rest could reflect workload management, particularly after a lengthy period away from game action, although the team has not confirmed that explanation.The timing made the move particularly noticeable: Hellebuyck had only just made his first start for New Jersey after the trade saga that kept him away from regular game action in Winnipeg. Yet one lineup decision is not enough to conclude that the team’s plans have changed.The next meaningful indicator will be the Devils’ updates on Hellebuyck’s availability and his place in the upcoming rotation. Until New Jersey provides further details, the reason for his absence remains uncertain.For now, Allen’s start against Colorado gave the Devils an opportunity to rely on their goaltending depth while Hellebuyck rested away from the lineup. The move was unexpected given the timing of his return, but any conclusions about an injury or a deeper issue would go beyond the confirmed information.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 7 NFL teams with best chance to win Super Bowl LXI entering Week 8
articles.summary: Week 7 finally knocked some shine off the NFL‘s heavyweights. San Francisco lost its perfect record in a four-turnover mess. Kansas City managed three points...
articles.body:
Week 7 finally knocked some shine off the NFL 's heavyweights. San Francisco lost its perfect record in a four-turnover mess. Kansas City managed three points against Seattle. Cincinnati buried Baltimore with 35 unanswered points. Minnesota remained unbeaten while somehow making a 16-10 victory feel like another warning about its offense. The championship picture didn't get turned upside down, but a few cracks became considerably harder to ignore.

That's the difference between ranking good teams and identifying legitimate Super Bowl contenders. Quarterback play, protection, defensive resilience, and the ability to win multiple ways matter more than collecting impressive Sundays. A great record can hide a serious weakness. One ugly loss can expose a problem without erasing six weeks of evidence.

Minnesota beat Indianapolis 16-10, and Brian Flores' defense practically dragged the offense across the finish line. The Vikings held the Colts to 64 net passing yards while blitzing on an extraordinary 85.2 percent of dropbacks.

Kyler Murray delivered the decisive late scramble, but threw for just 150 yards against a two-win opponent. The defense leads the league in EPA allowed per play, while the offense ranks 29th. Aaron Jones' aggravated MCL injury and declining blocking depth only complicate an attack already dependent on isolated moments of quarterback improvisation.

Detroit is next, giving Flores a fascinating matchup against one of the league's most efficient offenses. Buffalo and San Francisco loom in November, providing even better tests of Minnesota's offensive limitations. There's plenty to respect about a 6-0 team with a defense capable of suffocating almost anybody.

But championships generally demand more than asking that defense to perform a rescue operation every Sunday. Until Murray and the offense produce something more sustainable, Minnesota's undefeated record isn't enough to move it higher.

Cincinnati's 35-13 demolition of Baltimore was a reminder of how quickly Joe Burrow can hijack a football game. Trailing 13-0, the Bengals scored touchdowns on five consecutive possessions, with Burrow completing 16 of 18 passes for 249 yards and four touchdowns after halftime.

Tee Higgins contributed 148 receiving yards, and improved tackle protection is helping Burrow exploit a receiving corps that already terrifies defenses. The concern is an inefficient rushing attack and a defense that remains vulnerable to quarterback mobility and perimeter breakdowns. Beating Tyler Huntley doesn't answer every question about stopping elite opponents.

Tennessee visits Sunday, giving Cincinnati an opportunity to establish control without another spectacular comeback. Atlanta follows in Madrid, while Pittsburgh, Kansas City and a Baltimore rematch will provide more meaningful championship tests.

Cincinnati climbs because Burrow's passing game offers a reliable January scoring formula, especially with Chase and Higgins healthy. The Bengals don't have the defensive consistency or complementary rushing identity of the teams above them, but they're becoming considerably more dangerous as their protection improves.

Previous: Unranked | Back in the top seven

Seattle didn't merely beat Kansas City. It embarrassed an offense that rarely experiences anything resembling a helpless Sunday. The Seahawks held Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs to 213 yards, 11 first downs and zero red-zone possessions in a 20-3 victory.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba delivered 150 receiving yards, Emanuel Wilson rushed for 100 and Mike Macdonald's defense looked capable of dismantling anybody. The concern is whether the offense can repeat its contribution. Seattle still ranks 24th in offensive EPA per play, and Sam Darnold's end-zone interception was another reminder that turnovers and inconsistent protection haven't disappeared.

Acquiring All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson, pending his physical, could address a major weakness. He's allowed no sacks in 275 pass-blocking snaps this season, although he obviously had nothing to do with Sunday's victory. Chicago visits Monday, followed later by a San Francisco rematch and two remaining games against the Rams.

Those matchups will reveal whether Seattle's offense can become dependable enough to complement an elite defense. The Chiefs victory earns the Seahawks a return to the top seven. Sustaining that offensive improvement is what could make this team genuinely frightening in January.

Jacksonville rested in Week 7, leaving its 34-31 loss to Houston in London as the latest evidence. Trevor Lawrence threw for 306 yards and four touchdowns, but a costly end-zone interception and 426 yards allowed exposed problems that an explosive offense couldn't overcome.

Losing left tackle Anton Harrison to a season-ending ACL injury makes protection a substantial concern, particularly with Walker Little taking over. The defense remains excellent against the run, but its coverage hasn't been nearly as convincing. Jacksonville has enough offensive talent to threaten anybody; protecting Lawrence and preventing explosive passes are now the questions.

Indianapolis is up first before a Thursday trip to Baltimore, where the reshuffled offensive line gets to work. Chicago and a looming Houston rematch await later. Jacksonville is fourth in offensive EPA per play and seventh defensively, which reflects real chops more so than just one outstanding afternoon.

Liam Coen has built a versatile attack, and the defense provides enough resistance to survive an imperfect offense. That balance real, even if the occasional defensive lapses keep their championship case from feeling locked.

Buffalo enjoyed a Week 7 bye after beating Las Vegas 33-30, a game that perfectly captured the Bills' championship argument and its biggest problem. Josh Allen threw for 255 yards and two touchdowns without an interception, while James Cook contributed 153 yards from scrimmage. Buffalo scored on seven of nine meaningful possessions and continues to lead the league in offensive EPA per play.

Unfortunately, the defense ranks dead last in EPA allowed. The Raiders nearly erased a comfortable deficit, reinforcing the concern that Allen might spend January trying to rescue a defense incapable of protecting his work.

Baltimore visits Sunday with Lamar Jackson potentially returning, an immediate examination of Buffalo's defensive discipline. Minnesota's aggressive pressure awaits the following week, with Kansas City on Thanksgiving and Denver on Christmas providing additional playoff-caliber challenges.

Allen and Cook give Buffalo an extraordinary offensive ceiling, capable of winning through explosive passes, sustained drives, or a productive rushing attack. That's a championship foundation. But the Bills remain third because they haven't demonstrated the defensive reliability necessary to make that offense anything other than their primary survival mechanism.

There's no respectable way to dress up Kansas City's 20-3 loss in Seattle. The Chiefs generated 213 yards, 11 first downs and failed to reach the red zone for the first time in Patrick Mahomes' 153 career starts, including the playoffs. Kenneth Walker managed 36 rushing yards, and the offense never found an alternative.

Rashee Rice's absence, Jaylon Moore's concussion and Josh Simmons' continued absence exposed how vulnerable the passing game becomes when receiver depth and protection deteriorate simultaneously. For a team accustomed to solving problems, Kansas City spent Sunday looking completely out of answers.

Denver is next, with Nik Bonitto presenting an immediate test of the same protection issues Seattle exploited. Buffalo, the Rams, Cincinnati and San Francisco remain on the schedule. Kansas City stays second because Mahomes, Andy Reid and Steve Spagnuolo still provide one of football's strongest championship combinations.

The Chiefs rank fifth in both offensive and defensive EPA per play, and their defense remains capable of controlling games without demanding heroics from Mahomes. Seattle exposed a serious weakness, but one disastrous afternoon doesn't erase a season of excellent two-way football. It does eliminate much of Kansas City's margin for error.

San Francisco finally lost, falling 29-20 in Atlanta despite outgaining the Falcons 400-295. Four turnovers were the difference, including two Brock Purdy interceptions that undermined an otherwise productive offense. The 49ers remain second in offensive EPA per play and top 10 defensively, but the injury situation is becoming increasingly uncomfortable.

Christian McCaffrey is dealing with a mild hamstring strain, Nick Bosa has knee and calf issues, and the receiving corps remains depleted. Acquiring DeForest Buckner should strengthen a battered defensive front, but roster reinforcements don't automatically solve the turnover problem or restore everyone's health.

The Week 8 bye arrives at an excellent time, with Las Vegas waiting November 8 before more demanding matchups against Minnesota, Seattle, the Rams and Kansas City. Those games will test whether Kyle Shanahan can preserve the offense's explosive versatility while injuries continue reshaping his personnel.

San Francisco remains No. 1 because Purdy's efficiency, strong protection, Shanahan's adaptability and a credible defense still represent the most complete championship combination in football. The Atlanta loss exposed real vulnerabilities, and the 49ers are no longer comfortably separated from the field. But through seven games, nobody has assembled a stronger overall case to win Super Bowl LXI.

A 13-0 halftime lead against Cincinnati became a 35-13 loss, with five consecutive Bengals touchdown drives exposing the defense. Lamar Jackson is expected back, but his ankle remains untested in live action. Interior-line injuries and coverage breakdowns make Baltimore difficult to trust until its quarterback returns and the defense shows some resilience.

Matthew Stafford threw three touchdowns while Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined for 192 rushing yards against Las Vegas. That's the offensive versatility Sean McVay needs. Unfortunately, Davante Adams' ruptured hamstring, Poona Ford's season-ending injury and uncertainty elsewhere on defense make this roster increasingly difficult to trust over a playoff run.

Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson are building something legitimate, and Chicago showed composure beating New England 30-24. Montez Sweat's return strengthens the defensive front. But protection, coverage discipline, and inconsistent efficiency remain concerns. Monday night's trip to Seattle offers a terrific opportunity to prove this team belongs with the established contenders.

Nik Bonitto generated 13 pressures against Arizona, and Denver's defense can absolutely dictate games. Bo Nix completed just 15 of 29 passes despite the 30-16 victory, again exposing an inconsistent passing attack. The Broncos have championship-caliber defensive traits. Their offense hasn't earned the same confidence, and Kansas City visits Sunday.
